Name: narrative_diversification
Title: Expanding Detection to Emerging Propaganda Narratives
Experiment: Use the LLM to generate a diverse set of plausible new propaganda narratives targeting Japan, beyond well-known historical or territorial disputes. Automatically generate search queries from these new narratives and evaluate the detection pipeline’s ability to surface previously unobserved or creative forms of propaganda. Assess the increase in coverage compared to a baseline limited to fixed, well-known narratives.

Name: scoring_prompt_refinement
Title: Optimizing LLM Scoring Prompts for Greater Precision
Experiment: Experiment with alternative scoring prompts for the LLM classifier (e.g., clarifying scale anchors, adding more explicit negative/neutral examples, and refining role instructions). Compare detection precision, recall, and hit rates using each prompt variant on a manually verified set of YouTube videos. Identify prompt features that lead to the most accurate and robust anti-Japan propaganda classification.

Name: multilingual_query_optimization
Title: Optimizing Multilingual Search Queries for Enhanced Propaganda Detection
Experiment: Develop a new function to generate and weight search queries in multiple languages based on the narrative context. Implement a feedback loop mechanism that uses detection results to iteratively refine and optimize query generation and weighting strategies. Evaluate the impact on the retrieval of anti-Japan propaganda by comparing detection rates and content diversity between single-language and multilingual approaches. Use metrics such as hit rate improvement and diversity of detected content to assess effectiveness.
